newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Plessey upbeat on Australian deal.
newsitem.headline: Plessey upbeat on Australian deal.

text.p: Plessey Corporation Ltd chief executive John Temple said on Thursday he was upbeat about long-term prospects following the acquisition of a 74 percent stake in the electronics division of Australian AWA Ltd .
"The acquisition will have no material impact on Plessey's earnings in the year to March 31, but the long-term prospects are promising," Temple said in a statement on Thursday.
Plessey announced earlier that it would buy the stake for A$20 million (72 million rand).
Temple said the deal had been motivated by increased South African exports through AWA's distribution channels, rationalisation of research and development and rand hedge earnings.
It would also globalise opportunities, particularly for the supply of essential infrastructure products into the rapidly growing developing markets of South-East Asia.

"AWA's portfolio of its own developed products complements Plessey's, giving the combined businesses the necessary critical mass to be worldplayers, particularly in the high growth Asia Pacific markets.
"This has been an area of focus by AWA for more than five years and more recently by Plessey through the interests we have established in Malaysia," he said.
He said the deal would provide for the establishment of a new company, Plessey Australia.
The deal would be funded through the offshore sale of new shares once a satisfactory due diligence review had been completed.

It would buy the AWA Centre operations at a discount to net tangible assets for a total of A$25 million. Plessey Corporation would pay A$20 million for 74 percent of the equity with the balance of the shareholding being taken up by RMB Australia Ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Rand Merchant Bank, which brokered the deal, and Marcel Corporate, an Australian corporte advisory group.

AWA's electronics division, known as AWA Centre, designs, manufactures and markets air navigation systems, traffic control systems and rural radio communications with 70 percent of its A$70 million (252 million rand) sales coming from exports, mainly to Asian markets.
It has an order book of more than A$60 million (216 million rand).
AWA Ltd managing director John Dougall said the deal was the final step in refocusing AWA Ltd into its chosen core entertainment and data communications business in Australia.
